stories.title: Celeste and TowerFall leave Xbox as their developer backs the BDS boycott
paragraphs: Celeste and TowerFall were removed from the Xbox storefront, with creator Maddy Thorson saying the decision supports the BDS boycott, according to saved reporting.

The move applies to two established indie games and joins other developer withdrawals from Xbox reported by GamesRadar. The collected evidence does not establish whether existing owners lose access or quantify any effect on sales.
The case shows how a political boycott can become a platform-distribution decision for independent developers. The saved results do not measure wider developer or player support.

scoreNotes.general: A visible storefront decision by the creator of two well-known indie games ties platform access to the BDS boycott, though the saved evidence does not measure sales or player response.
scoreNotes.heat: The decision affects two established games and is part of a wider reported set of Xbox withdrawals, but the collected results provide no audience or sales measure.
scoreNotes.time: The developer's delisting decision was reported on October 29, within the current 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: GamesRadar and Vidas Infinitas both report the delisting and its stated BDS rationale; no further details about sales effects are available in the saved results.

stories.title: Modern Warfare 4 draws 148,300 peak Twitch viewers at launch
paragraphs: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 reached a reported peak of 148,300 Twitch viewers on its October 23 launch day, according to Streams Charts.
Streams Charts says that release-day peak exceeded Counter-Strike and Dota's peaks on Twitch that day. This is a platform-specific attention snapshot, not evidence of sales or total players.
The result gives publishers and creators an early signal of livestream demand around the new release. The saved evidence does not compare the figure with earlier Call of Duty launches.

scoreNotes.general: A substantial launch-day Twitch audience offers a useful attention signal for a major release, with the limits of one platform and one point-in-time count.
scoreNotes.heat: Streams Charts reports a 148,300 peak and says the game topped Counter-Strike and Dota on release day; no sales or total-player count is established.
scoreNotes.time: The release-day audience was measured October 23 and reported October 26, within the preceding seven days but outside the fresh 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: The viewership figure comes from specialist audience tracking and the October 23 launch date is supported by Call of Duty's announcement; the metric is not a sales measure.
